# Nerack: reference for writing apps

Nerack is a declarative, protocol-agnostic framework for asynchronous network applications in C, built around self-contained systems. An app is a set of modules; each module declares resources, databases, routines, and events whose pipelines (ordered lists of steps) turn a request into a response. This file is complete: everything needed to write a Nerack app is here. Read Preferred style, Syntax, and Gotchas before writing code; use Signatures for exact field names.

## Mental model

- A module is any `.c` file containing `module(name){...}` (`todos/todos.c` declares `module(todos)`). It runs once at boot and registers declarations; Nerack finds modules by scanning the project.
- A module body holds `http()`/`rns()` resources, `<engine>()` databases, `routine()`, `publish()`/`subscribe()`, and `error()`/`repair()` handlers. There is no module-level middleware; cross-cutting steps go in a resource's `.all`.
- A request runs the resource's `.all` steps, then the pipeline for its verb. Each step completes before the next starts; a step that cannot deliver raises an error instead. A pipeline that ends without a response step returns an empty success (HTTP: empty 200).
- Context is a scoped key/value store that lives for one pipeline run (a request, a routine, or an event delivery). Scopes: bare names (app scope: values the app controls, including its own signed cookies), `input:x` (raw parameters), `client:x` (request headers, lowercase, `-` as `_`), `server:x` (`server:client_ip`, `server:method`, `server:path`, `server:url`), `env:x` (environment variables: configuration and secrets), and `error:x` (errors). `validate()` checks any key and promotes it to app scope unprefixed: `input:title` → `title`, `server:method` → `method`, `title` stays `title`. Never authorize on `input:` or `client:` values.
- A value is a string, a table of records (query and fetch results), a blob (raw bytes: uploads and `BLOB` columns, `{data, size}`), or an opaque C pointer set with `set_opaque()`. `{{key}}` interpolates strings and tables into SQL, templates, URLs, and headers; SQL also binds blobs as `BLOB`; opaque values are invisible to all of them.
- Steps read their inputs from context by key and write their outputs to context by key. Templates and SQL are not in context: they are assets, and a step's template key names an asset in that step's own namespace (`sqlite_query({"todos_db", "get_todos", ...})` runs `get_todos.sql`, `html("todos", ...)` renders `todos.html`). Assets read their `{{values}}` from context; nothing written to context can become a template or SQL.
- The core has no notion of HTTP. Protocols are modules: `http.h` (HTTP) and `rns.h` (Reticulum). One app can serve several protocols, sharing databases, routines, and events.
- C, compiled as C23 with clang blocks: `nullptr`, `bool`, `constexpr`, `auto`, `[[attributes]]`, designated initializers, `^(){...}`. App code never calls `malloc`/`free` or manages threads or locks.

## Preferred style

Write apps the Nerack way, not the way most frameworks do:
- Hypermedia first, on every protocol. Render on the server and send HTML (http) or Micron (rns). Forms use POST-redirect-GET; live updates are `datastar()` patches over a resource's `.sse` channel. Do not build JSON endpoints plus client-side rendering unless the consumer is an API client or a single-page app's backend-for-frontend.
- One module per domain slice (`todos`, `activity`), owning its databases, SQL, templates, resources, routines, and events. Modules communicate only through events (`publish`/`emit`/`subscribe`) and links to each other's pages (`{{url:module:resource}}`, `http_redirect_to()`), never by reading each other's databases or assets.
- Logic lives in steps: SQL in `.sql` assets, markup in templates, and only shaping or decisions in `run()`. Prefer a declarative step over C whenever one exists.
- A pipeline may cross protocols (an `rns()` POST can `datastar()`-patch browsers on an `http()` `.sse` channel) and mix databases (a shared Postgres for auth alongside a per-user SQLite via `{{user_id}}` in the connection string).

## Conventions

Not required, but use them: they make pipelines self-describing.
- Context key suffixes: `_s` for a rendered string (`html("todos", "todos_s")`), `_data` for a table result (`"todos_data"`), `_d` for a single-row table (a `RETURNING` row, or a `.map_context_key` row). Validated inputs and flags are bare (`title`, `is_urgent`).
- Database keys end in `_db` (`todos_db`). SQL asset names are verbs (`get_todos`, `create_todo`, `create_todos_table`); template names are nouns (`todos`, `todo_row`).
- Project layout:
```
.
├── main.c                      # module(main): shared resources such as home
├── layout.html        # root assets are shared by every module
├── todos/
│   ├── todos.c                 # module(todos)
│   ├── todos.html     # module assets are private to todos
│   ├── todos.mu       # same key, Micron engine, for rns()
│   ├── create_todos_table.sql
│   └── get_todos.sql
├── cookie_auth/                # override of the bundled cookie_auth module
│   ├── cookie_auth.c           # module(cookie_auth){ http("login", ...); } replaces its login
│   └── login.html     # replaces its login page
├── public/                     # served directly; reference with {{asset:file}}
└── vendor/                     # third-party C sources and vendor modules, compiled and linked with the app
```

## Syntax

- Every call is a macro over a struct literal. Leading values are positional in struct-field order (see Signatures); the rest are named. `sqlite_query({"todos_db","get_todos","todos_data"})` equals `sqlite_query({.database_key="todos_db", .template_key="get_todos", .context_key="todos_data"})`. Name anything past the obvious leading fields.
- List steps take one `{...}` item per entry, and multiple items run concurrently: `validate`, `sqlite_query` (any `*_query`), `http_fetch`, `http_headers`, `http_cookies`. Write `validate({"input:title", not_empty_valid})`, never `validate("title", not_empty_valid)`.
- All other steps take their fields directly: `html("todos", "todos_s")`, `http_response("todos_s")`, `datastar("room", .target = "#messages")`.
- A pipeline is a brace list of steps separated by commas: `.get = { step, step, step }`. Module-level declarations are statements ending in `;`.
- Handler lists are `{code, {steps}}` entries: `.errors = {{http_bad_request, {http_reroute("todos")}}}`. Module-level: `error(http_not_found, {steps});`.
- Every step also accepts `.if_context_key`, `.unless_context_key`, `.map`, `.map_context_key` (per item for list steps).

## Signatures

Exact fields in positional order. `{...}` marks a nested list; `, ...` marks a list step.
```c
// nerack.h: core
module(name){ ... }
routine(.routine_key, {.steps}, .errors, .repairs, .accepts = {"key", ...});
error(.code, {.steps});                                       // module-scoped handler
repair(.code, {.steps});
text_template(.template_key, .template);                      // <key>.txt declared in code, as if beside the .c
sql_template(.template_key, .template);                       // <key>.sql declared in code
validate({.context_key, .regex, .error_message, .optional, .default_value, .types = {"image/png", ...}, .max_bytes}, ...)
join(.parent_context_key, .parent_field_key, .child_context_key, .child_field_key, .parent_child_join_key)
run(.icall = ^(){ ... })  |  run(.call = fn)                 // icall is positional: run(^(){ ... })
run_worker(.icall)  |  run_worker(.call = fn)
run_routine(.key)
nest({.steps})
text(.template_key, .context_key)                             // plain-text Mustache, <key>.txt
context(.context_key, .template)                              // step form of format(): literal template, no escaping

// sqlite.h (other engines: postgres.h, mysql.h, redis.h, duckdb.h, same shape)
sqlite(.database_key, .connection, {.migrations}, {.seeds});
sqlite_query({.database_key, .template_key, .context_key, .error_on_empty}, ...)

// http.h
http(.name, .url, .mime, .errors, .repairs, .all, .get, .post, .put, .patch, .delete, .sse = {.channel, {.steps}});
html_template(.template_key, .template);                      // <key>.html declared in code
markdown_template(.template_key, .template);                  // <key>.md declared in code
html(.template_key, .context_key)                             // Mustache
markdown(.template_key, .context_key)                         // Markdown with Mustache
json(.table_key, .context_key)                                // serialize the context table at table_key; numbers/booleans from SQL columns or fetched JSON stay typed, the rest are strings
http_response(.context_key, .status, .mime)
http_file_response(.table_key)                                // one-row table: data, type, name
http_fetch({.method, .url, .context_key, .json_table_key, .json, .text, .headers = {{"Name", "value"}, ...}}, ...)
http_sse(.channel, .event, .comment, .data = {"line", ...})
http_headers({.key, .value}, ...)
http_cookies({.key, .value}, {.key[, .value]}, ...)           // first pair is the cookie, the rest attributes
http_redirect(.key)                                           // resource in this module
http_redirect_to(.module_key, .resource_key)                  // resource in another module
http_redirect_external(.url)                                  // off-site 302; values after ? percent-encoded
http_reroute(.key)

// rns.h
rns(.name, .url, .errors, .repairs, .all, .get, .post, .put, .patch, .delete);
micron_template(.template_key, .template);                    // <key>.mu declared in code
micron(.template_key, .context_key)
rns_response(.context_key)
rns_reroute(.key)

// pubsub.h
publish(.event, .with = {"key", ...});                       // event names are global: "todo_created"
subscribe(.event, {.steps}, .errors, .repairs);               // by event name, never the publishing module
emit(.key)                                                    // only events this module publishes

// task.h
dispatch(.key)
cron(.routine_key, .schedule);                                // module-level; dispatches the routine on schedule

// datastar.h: name every field after .channel (the second positional field is .elements)
datastar(.channel, .elements, .javascript, .target, .signals, .mode)

// auth.h (included by cookie_auth.h and rns_auth.h)
auth_user()                                                   // find or create user for verified email, set user_id

// cookie_auth.h
cookie_logged_in()  cookie_session()  cookie_login()  cookie_logout()  cookie_signup()  cookie_link()  cookie_sign_in()

// rns_auth.h (same users as cookie_auth)
rns_logged_in()  rns_session()  rns_login()  rns_signup()  rns_link()  rns_sign_in()

// htmx.h, tailwind.h, daisyui.h: no steps; partials {{> htmx}} {{> tailwind}} {{> daisyui}} (datastar.h adds {{> datastar}})
```

## Imperative API (inside run, run_worker, and .call functions)

```c
typedef char const * const string;
typedef struct { int const code; string const message; } error;
typedef struct { void const * const data; size_t const size; } blob;   // get()/record_get() on a blob value returns a blob_handle
// table_handle, record_handle: opaque handles; blob_handle: blob const*

void*  get(string key);                       // nullptr if absent; caller knows the type
void   set_string(string key, string value);
void   set_table(string key, table_handle t);
void   set_blob(string key, blob_handle b);   // raw bytes {data, size}; SQL binds as BLOB
void   set_opaque(string key, void const * p); // opaque; invisible to templates and SQL
       // set_* never copy: the value (and a blob's data) must outlive the run; new blobs via blob_new(), never &(blob){...}
bool   has(string key);
void   format(string key, string tmpl);       // resolve {{...}} in a literal (no escaping, no {{url:}}/{{sse:}}), write to key

void*  alloc(size_t bytes);                   // arena, freed when the pipeline run ends
void   defer_free(void const * p);            // free a library-owned pointer at run end

void   error_set(string key, error e);        // raise; nearest error/repair pipeline runs
error  error_get(string key);
bool   error_has(string key);

table_handle  table_new();
size_t        table_length(table_handle t);
record_handle table_get(table_handle t, size_t i);   // nullptr if out of range
void          table_add(table_handle t, record_handle r);
void          table_remove(table_handle t, record_handle r);
void          table_remove_at(table_handle t, size_t i);

record_handle record_new();
void*         record_get(record_handle r, string key);   // nullptr if absent
void          record_set_string(record_handle r, string key, string value);
void          record_set_table(record_handle r, string key, table_handle t);
void          record_set_blob(record_handle r, string key, blob_handle b);
void          record_set_opaque(record_handle r, string key, void const * p);
void          record_remove(record_handle r, string key);

blob_handle   blob_new(void const * data, size_t size); // arena-held {data, size}; data not copied
```
Third-party C goes in `vendor/` and is called from `run_worker()`; register its allocations with `defer_free()`. A folder in `vendor/` holding a `module()` (source, or `name.h` plus the compiled library) is a vendor module: shared across apps, sees only its own assets, can override bundled modules by shipping a same-named module in its folder, and reuses bundled steps (an SSO module ships `cookie_auth/cookie_auth.c` replacing `login`, and its callback calls `auth_user()` + `cookie_sign_in()`).

## Step semantics

- `validate` checks context keys of any scope; request parameters (query, form, JSON-body top-level keys, URL params) are `input:name`. On success each value is promoted to app scope unprefixed; on failure it writes `error:name` and raises `err_invalid` (400). All items validate before the error fires, so every field error surfaces together. For checks beyond regex (uniqueness, cross-field), follow it with a query and a `run()` that calls `error_set()`. Files use `.types` (checked against the sniffed type) and `.max_bytes` instead of `.regex`.
- Uploads: each multipart file field is `input:<field>`, a one-row table `{name (client filename, untrusted), type (sniffed), size, data (blob)}`, held in memory for the run only; over `env:max_upload_bytes` (default 10 MB) → `err_invalid`. Store it with SQL (`{{#avatar}}insert ... values ({{name}}, {{type}}, {{data}}){{/avatar}}`) and serve it with `http_file_response("avatar_d")` from a `select name, type, data` row: sets the type, `nosniff`, and `Content-Disposition` (inline for non-SVG images, attachment otherwise). `public/` is embedded in the production binary and never written at runtime.
- `*_query` runs the SQL asset `<.template_key>.sql`. SQL assets are full Mustache (sections, partials, helpers: `{{#filter}}and status = {{filter}}{{/filter}}`), but every `{{x}}` (and `{{{x}}}`/`{{&x}}`) becomes a bound placeholder, never spliced text; an absent `{{x}}` binds NULL; a table expands to one placeholder per row from its first column (`id in ({{ids}})`). Multi-row insert: `begin; {{#tags}}insert into tags (todo_id, name) values ({{todo_id}}, {{name}});{{/tags}} commit;` in one asset, atomic. The result is always a table, even for one row; omit `.context_key` when unused. `.error_on_empty` raises `err_not_found` (404) on zero rows affected or returned. Each asset runs atomically and in isolation: transactions are `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` inside one asset, never across steps or items; a failure or an unclosed transaction rolls back. A multi-statement script returns the last row-returning statement.
- `join` nests each parent record's matching children under a new field (default: the child table's key). `{blog:[{id}], comments:[{blog_id}]}` becomes `{blog:[{id, comments:[...]}]}`.
- `run` executes short, non-blocking C on the reactor. `run_worker` executes on the shared thread pool for blocking or CPU-bound work and resumes the pipeline on the original reactor.
- `nest` groups steps so one `.if_context_key`/`.unless_context_key` covers them all.
- `run_routine` runs a routine inline; `dispatch` enqueues it as a task (a durable background job) and continues immediately.
- `http_fetch` makes outbound requests; JSON responses parse into tables and records, text into strings. `.json` is a literal body whose values are JSON-escaped as string contents (write `"{{title}}"` in quotes; numbers/booleans from SQL or JSON may stand bare); `.json_table_key` names a context value serialized as the body; `.text` names a context string sent as the body. In `.url`, as in `http_redirect_external()`, values after `?` are percent-encoded.
- Header and cookie values (`http_headers`, `http_cookies`) interpolate; a value with CR, LF, or NUL raises `err_internal`. In `http_sse`, a `.data` value with line breaks continues on further `data:` lines; a line break in `.event`/`.comment` raises `err_internal`.
- `context(key, template)` renders a literal template into `key` like `format()` (no escaping); unlike `format()`, it is known at boot, so `{{url:}}`/`{{sse:}}` in it fail the boot.
- `text`/`html`/`markdown`/`micron` render the asset `<.template_key>.txt`/`.html`/`.md`/`.mu` into `.context_key`; `{{x}}` is escaped for the output (HTML, Micron markup), except in `text`. `json` serializes the context table under `.table_key` (not an asset).
- `http_response` sends a context value; `.status` defaults to `http_ok`, `.mime` to the resource's `.mime`.
- `http_redirect` returns a 302 to a resource in its own module, `http_redirect_to("module", "resource")` to another module's; `http_reroute`/`rns_reroute` re-enter the router in process and run the target's `.all` and GET pipeline. All of them fill the target's `:params` from context by matching key names.
- `http_sse` broadcasts to every client on `.channel`, or to the requester when `.channel` is omitted. Each call writes its components straight to the connection, so consecutive calls build one record.
- `datastar` patches the HTML under `.elements` into `.target` (id or CSS selector, interpolates) for every client on `.channel`, or only the requesting client when `.channel` is omitted (validation errors), using `.mode` (default `outer_mode`; `remove_mode` needs no `.elements`). `.signals` names a one-row table whose fields merge into the client's signals (serialized like `json()`); `.javascript` runs on the client.
- `.map = "table"` runs the step once per row, all rows concurrently, with the row's fields in scope as bare `{{field}}`; with a result key, outputs collect into a table aligned to the input. `.map_context_key = "k"` also exposes the row as the single-row table `k`, for fields that take a table key (`.json_table_key`, `json()`).
- `.if_context_key = "k"` runs the step only when `k` is true; `.unless_context_key` only when false. False: missing, `nullptr`, `""`, `"0"`, `"false"`, or a table with no rows; everything else is true (opaque values too). Template sections use the same rule, except opaque values are false there. Works with any key, including `is_htmx`, `is_datastar`, and flags set in `run()`.

## Resources

- `http()` declares a resource, not a route. Its name is used by `{{url:module:resource}}`, `{{sse:module:resource}}`, `http_redirect()`, `http_redirect_to()`, and `http_reroute()`, and is unique among the module's `http()` resources; URL patterns are unique per protocol app-wide. An exact path beats a parameterized one regardless of order. The verb comes from the HTTP method, or from a `_method` field on a POST. `.mime` defaults to `mime_html`.
- `.sse = {"channel:{{interp}}", {steps}}` opens a persistent SSE channel; browsers connect with `{{sse:module:resource}}` (a GET). The steps run on connect, after `.all`. `.sse = {"room"}` with no steps just subscribes.
- `rns()` has the same fields as `http()` except `.mime` and `.sse`. Pages are Micron, rendered by `micron()`. Link fields (`|title`) and `:params` arrive as `input:<name>`; `server:method`/`path`/`url` are set; there is no `client:` scope and no `server:client_ip`. Auth comes from `rns_auth.h` (`rns_logged_in()`, `rns_session()`), the only way the peer's identity reaches the app.
- Resource names are per module and per protocol: the same module can have `http("room", ...)` and `rns("room", ...)`, and two modules can each have a `home`. Templates always name the module (`{{url:todos:todos}}`). `http_redirect`/`http_reroute`/`rns_reroute` take a resource of their own module; only `http_redirect_to("todos", "todos")` reaches another module.

## Assets

Every non-`.c` file is an asset, keyed by its basename up to the first dot: `get_todos.sql` → `get_todos`, `todos.html` → `todos`. Each step has its own namespace, its file type: `text()` reads `<key>.txt`, `html()` `<key>.html`, `markdown()` `<key>.md`, `micron()` `<key>.mu`, `*_query()` and `.migrations`/`.seeds` `<key>.sql`; one key can name a file for each. `{{> partial}}` and `{{< parent}}` resolve in the namespace of the step rendering the enclosing template. Assets are never context values and context values are never assets; a template key with no matching asset fails at boot. `text_template()`, `sql_template()`, `html_template()`, `markdown_template()`, and `micron_template()` declare an asset in code (`html_template("todo_row", ...)` registers `todo_row.html`), exactly as if `<key>.<type>` sat beside the declaring `.c` file; a declaration and a file with the same key and type in one folder fail the boot. The scan skips dotfiles/dot-folders, `dev/`, `prod/`, `public/`, `vendor/`, and `LICENSE` files (every `.md`, `README.md` included, is an asset). Lookup order: the module's own folder, each folder up to the project root (root assets are shared, a module folder's are private, never sideways; a folder without its own `module()` belongs to the folder above), then the bundled/vendor modules it includes (`{{> htmx}}`). Replace a bundled or vendor module's asset from an override module (a folder named after it, with `module(name){}`); dev and the production binary resolve them identically. `public/` files are served directly and referenced with `{{asset:file}}`.

## Templates

Mustache, auto-escaped for the output (HTML in `html`/`markdown`, Micron markup in `micron`; `text()` does not escape). The full base spec except dot notation:
`{{x}}` escaped · `{{{x}}}`/`{{&x}}` raw · `{{#x}}..{{/x}}` section/loop · `{{^x}}..{{/x}}` inverted · `{{! c }}` comment · `{{=<% %>=}}` delimiters · `{{> name}}` partial · `{{< parent}}{{$block}}override{{/block}}{{/parent}}` inheritance (any template with a `{{$block}}default{{/block}}` can be a parent; layouts are built this way).
A missing key, `nullptr`, or a value templates can't render (opaque, blob) renders empty and its section is falsy; only the unrenderable case is logged.

Helpers (`{{helper:args}}`, colon-separated; each arg is a literal or a context key):
- `{{url:module:resource}}`: resource URL; `:params` fill from the current scope by key name, so it works per row inside a section. `{{url:todos:todos:filter=done}}` → `/todos?filter=done`. Always name the module, even your own (the first two segments are module and resource; the rest are arguments), so templates work unchanged as shared layouts or partials; bundled/vendor resources too: `{{url:cookie_auth:login}}`. Resolves among `http()` resources in `html`/`markdown`, `rns()` in `micron`; only those templates (and `http_redirect_external()`'s `.url`) take `{{url:}}`/`{{sse:}}` (in `text` or SQL assets and `context()` they fail the boot; in `format()` they raise `err_internal`).
- `{{method:verb}}`: hidden `_method` field so a POST form reaches `put`/`patch`/`delete` (`<input type='hidden' name='_method' value='delete'>`). In Micron it renders a `_method=<verb>` link field and is needed for every non-GET verb, `post` included: `` `[add`{{url:todos:todos}}`{{method:post}}|title] ``. Datastar and htmx send the real method and need no helper.
- `{{sse:module:resource}}`: `{{url:module:resource}}` plus `_method=sse`, the GET that connects to `.sse`.
- `{{input:field}}` raw parameter for repopulating forms · `{{error:field}}` section, truthy on error · `{{error_message:field}}` · `{{error_code:field}}` · `{{precision:field:N}}` N decimals · `{{asset:file}}` cache-busted `public/` URL.
- Datastar attributes use the colon form: `data-bind:title`, `data-on:click="@post('{{url:todos:todos}}')"`, `data-init="@get('{{sse:todos:todos}}')"`.

## Errors & repairs

Lookup by code: the resource's (or routine's, or subscriber's) `.errors`/`.repairs` first, then the module's `error()`/`repair()`. Repairs resolve before errors. A repair fixes context, then the failed step reruns (only its failed items) and the pipeline continues; a second failure with the same code goes to errors, a failure inside a repair goes to errors, and repairs never respond; a request's error handler responds, and every error handler ends the run. Unhandled errors render the asset named after the code in the protocol's format (`404.html`, `404.mu`) if present, else the message as plain text, with that status. Core codes: `err_invalid` 400, `err_unauthorized` 401, `err_not_found` 404, `err_internal` 500; `http.h` aliases `http_bad_request`, `http_not_authorized`, `http_not_found`, `http_error`. Custom: `#define err_quota 723`.

## Events, routines, and tasks

- Events (`pubsub.h`) are durable: undelivered events replay after a crash. Names are global, one publisher per name; subscribers name only the event. `publish` declares the event and the keys it carries; `emit` fires it; each `subscribe` in any module receives those keys. Adding a subscriber never changes the publisher.
- Routines are named, reusable pipelines. `run_routine` runs one inline. `dispatch` (`task.h`) runs it as a task, durably on the task reactor: checkpointed after each step, resumed after a crash. `cron("name", "0 8 * * *")` (`task.h`, module-level) dispatches it on a schedule, so scheduled runs are durable; missed runs while down run once at boot; a run still in progress makes the next tick skip. `.accepts` lists caller keys copied into the routine's context.

## Bundled modules

- `htmx.h`: `{{> htmx}}` partial; sets `is_htmx` on `HX-Request`.
- `datastar.h`: `{{> datastar}}` partial and `datastar()`. Sets `is_datastar` on its requests and puts their signals (JSON body, or the `datastar` query parameter on GET) into `input:` for `validate()`.
- `tailwind.h`, `daisyui.h`: `{{> tailwind}}`, `{{> daisyui}}` in `<head>`; classes used in templates compile automatically.
- `auth.h` (included by `cookie_auth.h` and `rns_auth.h`): the user store (id, unique email, short name, salted password hash, link codes); sessions live in `cookie_auth`, bound identities in `rns_auth`, all keyed by `user_id`. Publishes `user_created`, `user_credentials_changed` (cookie_auth deletes stale session rows), and `user_deleted` (front ends drop sessions/identities; apps can `subscribe("user_deleted", ...)` to delete their own rows), each with `user_id`; delivery is durable and async. One user across protocols: `user_id` is the same in `http()` and `rns()` pipelines. Steps from a bundled module resolve names in that module, so `cookie_session()` reads users through `auth` while the app cannot name its database. `auth_user()` finds or creates the user for a verified `email` (new users take `short_name`, have no password) and sets `user_id`; never feed it a form value. Pair with `cookie_sign_in()` (sets the signed cookie for `user_id`) or `rns_sign_in()` (binds the identified peer to `user_id`); both end the pipeline by returning the visitor to the page that needed sign-in (or `/`), so no redirect step follows. To move users to another engine (a shared Postgres), override `auth` (`auth/auth.c`: `module(auth){ postgres("auth_db", "{{env:auth_database_url}}", {...}); }`, migrations in that folder); `cookie_auth_db` and `rns_auth_db` move the same way.
- `cookie_auth.h`: including it mounts `/login`, `/logout`, `/signup`, `/account` and their pages. `cookie_link()` (the `/account` action) issues a one-time `link_code` (single use, 10 minutes) for linking a Reticulum identity. Sessions are server-side in `cookie_auth`'s own database: the signed `HttpOnly` cookie holds a random session id; sliding expiry `env:session_days` (30, renewed at most daily), hard cap `env:session_max_days` (90); one session per device; logout deletes it server-side; a password change ends the others instantly (sessions started before the user's `credentials_changed_at` are rejected; the changing request gets a fresh session). `cookie_logged_in()` gates: with a live session it sets `user_id`, else redirects through login; it does not load the user. `cookie_session()` sets `user_id` and loads `user` when signed in (`id`, `email`, `short_name`: `{{#user}}{{short_name}}{{/user}}`). Users live in `auth`; apps never query it. Ownership is the app's job: scope SQL with `and user_id = {{user_id}}` plus `.error_on_empty = true` (404 for another user's row). Cookies are signed with `env:cookie_secret` (random in dev when unset). Use either or both, in `.all` or a verb. `cookie_login()`/`cookie_logout()`/`cookie_signup()`/`cookie_link()` are the actions. Customize it with an override module, a `cookie_auth/` folder with `module(cookie_auth){...}`: `login`/`signup`/`account.html` there restyle a page; `http("login", ...)` (or `logout`, `signup`, `account`) there replaces a resource and must call the action. Link with `{{url:cookie_auth:login}}`; logout is a POST form to `{{url:cookie_auth:logout}}`.
- `rns_auth.h`: a Reticulum identity is a credential bound to an `auth` user, like a passkey. Mounts `login`, `signup`, `link` (`/login`, `/signup`, `/link`; `{{url:rns_auth:login}}`) with Micron pages. An identified peer binds by signing up, logging in with email/password, or entering a `cookie_link()` code. `rns_logged_in()` gates: sets `user_id` when the identity is bound, else responds with the login page (anonymous peers are asked to identify) and returns afterwards. `rns_session()` loads `user` when bound and never fails. No logout: a peer signs out by not identifying. `rns_login()`/`rns_signup()`/`rns_link()` are the actions; customize them the same way from an `rns_auth/` override module.
- Databases: `sqlite` is bundled; other engines are modules of the same shape. Migrations and seeds are forward-only and index-based: each runs once, in array order, tracked in `nerack_meta`; append new ones at the end. Interpolation in `.connection` makes a database multi-tenant.

## Constants

Verbs: `http_get http_post http_put http_patch http_delete`.
Status: `http_ok`200 `http_created`201 `http_redirected`302 `http_bad_request`400 `http_not_authorized`401 `http_not_found`404 `http_error`500.
Mime: `mime_html mime_text mime_event_stream mime_json mime_javascript`.
Datastar modes: `outer_mode inner_mode replace_mode prepend_mode append_mode before_mode after_mode remove_mode`.
Validators (`nerack.h`): `not_empty_valid alpha_valid alphanumeric_valid slug_valid integer_valid positive_integer_valid float_valid percent_valid email_valid uuid_valid user_valid date_valid time_valid datetime_valid zip_valid phone_valid cron_valid token_valid base64_valid bool_valid yes_no_valid on_off_valid`; (`http.h`): `no_html_valid url_valid ipv4_valid hex_color_valid`. Custom: `#define sku_valid "^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$"`.

## Gotchas

- List steps need inner braces: `validate({"input:title", not_empty_valid})`, `sqlite_query({...})`, `http_fetch({...})`.
- No dot notation in templates: `{{#a}}{{b}}{{/a}}`, never `{{a.b}}`.
- Regex is POSIX extended: `[0-9]` and `[[:space:]]`, never `\d` or `\s`.
- Each module is self-contained: every name it declares is its own, and databases, routines, assets, and handlers resolve only within it. Only resources (`{{url:module:resource}}`, `{{sse:module:resource}}`, `http_redirect_to("module", "resource")`) and events (global names, only the keys in `publish()`) cross modules; reroutes stay within the module. Context is the one shared namespace. Override a bundled or vendor module by declaring a module of the same name in a folder of that name (tiers: bundled < vendor < app; the higher tier wins, two same-tier overrides fail the boot): same-named resources (per protocol), assets (key and type), routines, and handlers replace the original's, new names are added, it runs as that module, a database declared under the original's key replaces it (any engine; its migrations must create the tables the module's queries expect), and it cannot redeclare the original's published events. App modules cannot be overridden. Every referenced name is checked at boot (template keys → assets, database keys → databases, routine, resource, and event names); an unknown name, a `{{url:}}`/`{{sse:}}` without its module, or any name for another module's database, routine, asset, or handler fails the boot.
- Context keys are global to the pipeline run: give every output a distinct key, or a later step overwrites it.
- A template key names an asset, never a context value: `{{todos}}` in a template is context data, not `todos.html`. Inline templates are still assets: `*_template()` declares one under a key, and `context()`/`format()` take a string literal; never build a template from a context value.
- Includes: `text` is core; `html`/`markdown`/`json`/`http_*` need `http.h`; `micron`/`rns_*` need `rns.h` (`rns_logged_in`/`rns_session`/`rns_login`/`rns_signup`/`rns_link`/`rns_sign_in` need `rns_auth.h`); `cookie_*` need `cookie_auth.h`; `publish`/`subscribe`/`emit` need `pubsub.h`; `dispatch` and `cron` need `task.h`; `datastar` needs `datastar.h`.
- `http_reroute()`/`rns_reroute()` run the target's `.all` and GET pipeline, not the current verb, keeping the whole context and the handled error's status (400 after a failed `validate()`). Each resource's `.all` runs at most once per request; a reroute loop fails with `err_internal`.
- HTML forms reach `put`/`patch`/`delete` only with `{{method:verb}}`; Micron needs it for every non-GET verb.
- State-changing actions (logout, delete) are POST forms or Datastar actions, never plain links.
- A query result is always a table; enter it with `{{#todo_data}}...{{/todo_data}}` even for one row.
- `run()` runs on the reactor: keep it short and non-blocking; anything blocking goes in `run_worker()`.
- No `malloc`/`free`, threads, or locks in app code; use `alloc()` and `defer_free()`.

## Configuration

Environment variables (non-secret ones also as flags, `PORT` → `--port`; flag wins), each also readable as `env:<lowercase>`: `PORT` 3000 · `HTTP_REACTOR_COUNT` CPU cores · `WORKER_COUNT` CPU cores · `DATA_DIR` working dir (relative SQLite paths; Docker image uses `/data` volume) · `COOKIE_SECRET` random in dev, required in production when the app uses `http.h` (env only) · `TRUSTED_PROXIES` none (comma-separated IPs/CIDRs) · `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` 10485760 · `SESSION_DAYS` 30 · `SESSION_MAX_DAYS` 90 · `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` http://localhost:4318. One process uses the whole machine; SQLite files belong to that one process, so sharing data across processes needs a networked engine module. `nerack docker` writes the image plus a `compose.yml` (port 3000, `/data` volume, `env_file`).

## Testing

No built-in test runner yet. Test black-box: start `nerack` with `DATA_DIR=$(mktemp -d)` (fresh databases each run) and drive it over HTTP with Hurl (requests/responses; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE need an `Origin:` header matching the app, or the CSRF check rejects them) or Playwright (interaction tests: Datastar patches, htmx swaps; `page.goto`, fill, click, `expect(locator).toContainText`). Do not write C test harnesses against Nerack internals.

## Framework-handled (do not reimplement)

Per-run arena memory and bounds-checked structures (a missing key returns `nullptr`); SQL injection (bound parameters), XSS (auto-escaping), and CSRF (same-origin checks via `Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin`, `SameSite=Lax` cookies; no tokens or hidden fields; non-browser clients must send a matching `Origin` on state-changing requests); concurrency, threads, locks, and connection pooling; durable events and tasks; OpenTelemetry spans, logs, and errors per step; compilation, hot reload, and HMR.

## Recipes

```c
// Form with validation: POST-redirect-GET; on failure re-render GET, form repopulates from input:/error:
http("todos", "/todos",
  .get  = {sqlite_query({"todos_db", "get_todos", "todos_data"}), html("todos", "todos_s"), http_response("todos_s")},
  .post = {validate({"input:title", not_empty_valid, "cannot be empty"}), sqlite_query({"todos_db", "create_todo"}), http_redirect("todos")},
  .errors = {{http_bad_request, {http_reroute("todos")}}}
);

// Custom validation beyond regex
validate({"input:username", user_valid, "3–32 letters, digits, or _, starting with a letter"}),
sqlite_query({"users_db", "find_username", "existing_data"}),
run(^(){ if (table_length(get("existing_data")) > 0) error_set("username", (error){err_invalid, "already taken"}); }),

// Auth-gated resource with a per-user database
sqlite("notes_db", "file:{{user_id}}_notes.db?mode=rwc", {"create_notes_table"});
http("notes", "/notes", .all = {cookie_logged_in(), cookie_session()}, .get = { ... });

// htmx: fragment for htmx requests, full page otherwise
html("todos_fragment", "page_s", .if_context_key = "is_htmx"),
html("todos_page", "page_s", .unless_context_key = "is_htmx"),
http_response("page_s")

// JSON for an API client or SPA backend-for-frontend; non-browser clients send Origin: <app origin> on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE
http("api_todos", "/api/todos", .mime = mime_json,
  .get = {sqlite_query({"todos_db", "get_todos", "todos_data"}), json("todos_data", "todos_s"), http_response("todos_s")}
);

// Concurrent outbound calls, then a durable background job
http_fetch({http_get, "https://api.weather.dev/now", "weather_data"}, {http_get, "https://api.quotes.dev/random", "quote_data"}),
dispatch("notify_new_todo"),
routine("notify_new_todo", {http_fetch({http_post, "https://api.push.dev/notify", .json = "{\"text\":\"{{title}}\"}"})}, .accepts = {"title"});
routine("daily_digest", {sqlite_query({"todos_db", "digest"})});
cron("daily_digest", "0 8 * * *");

// Blocking third-party C on the thread pool
run_worker(^(){ char * const out = cmark_markdown_to_html(get("md"), strlen(get("md")), 0); defer_free(out); set_string("md_s", out); })
```

## Example: modules and events

```c
// todos/get_todos.sql    select id, title from todos;
// todos/get_todo.sql     select id, title from todos where id = {{id}};
// todos/get_comments.sql select id, todo_id, body from comments where todo_id = {{id}};
// todos/create_todo.sql  insert into todos(title) values({{title}});
// todos/todos.html
//   {{< layout}}{{$body}}
//     <form method='post' action='{{url:todos:todos}}'>
//       <input name='title' value='{{input:title}}'>
//       {{#error:title}}<span>{{error_message:title}}</span>{{/error:title}}
//     </form>
//     <ul>{{#todos_data}}<li><a href='{{url:todos:todo}}'>{{title}}</a></li>{{/todos_data}}</ul>
//   {{/body}}{{/layout}}

// todos/todos.c
#include <nerack.h>
#include <http.h>
#include <sqlite.h>
#include <pubsub.h>

module(todos){
  sqlite("todos_db", "file:todos.db?mode=rwc", {"create_todos_table"}, {"seed_todos"});
  publish("todo_created", .with = {"title"});

  http("todos", "/todos",
    .get = {
      sqlite_query({"todos_db", "get_todos", "todos_data"}),
      html("todos", "todos_s"),
      http_response("todos_s")
    },
    .post = {
      validate({"input:title", not_empty_valid, "cannot be empty"}),
      sqlite_query({"todos_db", "create_todo"}),
      emit("todo_created"),
      http_redirect("todos")                                  // POST-redirect-GET
    },
    .errors = {{http_bad_request, {http_reroute("todos")}}}   // re-render GET; form repopulates from input:/error:
  );

  http("todo", "/todos/:id",
    .all = {validate({"input:id", positive_integer_valid})},
    .get = {
      sqlite_query(                                           // both run concurrently
        {"todos_db", "get_todo", "todo_data", .error_on_empty = true},
        {"todos_db", "get_comments", "comments"}
      ),
      run(^(){                                                // shape data between steps
        table_handle const c = get("comments");
        if (table_length(c) > 10) set_string("is_popular", "1");   // template: {{#is_popular}}
      }),
      join("todo_data", "id", "comments", "todo_id"),
      html("todo", "todo_s"),
      http_response("todo_s")
    }
  );
}

// activity/activity.c: subscriber, no dependency on todos
#include <nerack.h>
#include <sqlite.h>
#include <pubsub.h>

module(activity){
  sqlite("activity_db", "file:activity.db?mode=rwc", {"create_activity_table"});
  subscribe("todo_created", {sqlite_query({"activity_db", "insert_activity"})});
}
```

## Example: live, cross-protocol chat room

A message posted from a browser (Datastar) or from an RNS peer (Micron) is stored once and appended live in every connected browser.
```c
// chat/create_messages_table.sql  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, body TEXT NOT NULL);
// chat/get_messages.sql           select id, body from messages order by id;
// chat/insert_message.sql         insert into messages(body) values({{body}}) returning id, body;
// chat/message.html      {{#message_d}}<li id='message-{{id}}'>{{body}}</li>{{/message_d}}
// chat/body_error.html   <p id='body_error'>{{error_message:body}}</p>
// chat/room.html
//   {{< layout}}{{$body}}
//     <ul id='messages' data-init="@get('{{sse:chat:room}}')">
//       {{#messages_data}}<li id='message-{{id}}'>{{body}}</li>{{/messages_data}}
//     </ul>
//     <input data-bind:body><button data-on:click="@post('{{url:chat:room}}')">Send</button>
//     <p id='body_error'></p>
//   {{/body}}{{/layout}}
// chat/room.mu
//   {{#messages_data}}{{body}}
//   {{/messages_data}}
//   `<body`>`[send`{{url:chat:room}}`{{method:post}}|body]

// chat/chat.c
#include <nerack.h>
#include <http.h>
#include <rns.h>
#include <sqlite.h>
#include <datastar.h>

module(chat){
  sqlite("chat_db", "file:chat.db?mode=rwc", {"create_messages_table"});

  http("room", "/room",
    .sse = {"room"},                                          // browsers listen here for patches
    .get = {
      sqlite_query({"chat_db", "get_messages", "messages_data"}),
      html("room", "room_s"),
      http_response("room_s")
    },
    .post = {                                                 // Datastar signals arrive in input:
      validate({"input:body", not_empty_valid, "cannot be empty"}),
      sqlite_query({"chat_db", "insert_message", "message_d", .error_on_empty = true}),
      html("message", "message_s"),
      datastar("room", .target = "#messages", .mode = append_mode, .elements = "message_s")
    },                                                        // no response step: empty 200; the patch is the output
    .errors = {{http_bad_request, {                           // error goes only to the sender: no channel
      html("body_error", "body_error_s"),
      datastar(.target = "#body_error", .elements = "body_error_s")
    }}}
  );

  rns("room", "/room",
    .get = {
      sqlite_query({"chat_db", "get_messages", "messages_data"}),
      micron("room", "room_s"),
      rns_response("room_s")
    },
    .post = {
      validate({"input:body", not_empty_valid, "cannot be empty"}),
      sqlite_query({"chat_db", "insert_message", "message_d", .error_on_empty = true}),
      html("message", "message_s"),                           // render HTML for the browsers
      datastar("room", .target = "#messages", .mode = append_mode, .elements = "message_s"),
      rns_reroute("room")                                     // and Micron back to the RNS peer
    }
  );
}
```
